question: 76 × 2 − (33 + 15) + 58 − 49 + 27 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 140.

GIVEN

• 76 × 2 − (33 + 15) + 58 − 49 + 27

SOLUTION

• Brackets: (33 + 15) = 48

• Multiply: 76 × 2 = 152

• 152 − 48 + 58 − 49 + 27 = 152 − 48 = 104; 104 + 58 = 162; 162 − 49 = 113; 113 + 27 = 140.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group signs: positives 152 + 58 + 27 = 237, negatives 48 + 49 = 97, so 237 − 97 = 140. Fast and error-free.

NOTE

• Always apply BODMAS: Brackets → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction, left to right for same-priority operators.

question: 91 − 33 + 42 ÷ 6 + (18 of 3) − 29 + 22 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 112.

GIVEN

• 91 − 33 + 42 ÷ 6 + (18 of 3) − 29 + 22

SOLUTION

• 'of' and division first: 18 of 3 = 18 × 3 = 54; 42 ÷ 6 = 7

• 91 − 33 + 7 + 54 − 29 + 22 = 91 − 33 = 58; 58 + 7 = 65; 65 + 54 = 119; 119 − 29 = 90; 90 + 22 = 112.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 91 + 7 + 54 + 22 = 174; negatives: 33 + 29 = 62; 174 − 62 = 112.

NOTE

• 'of' behaves like multiplication and is resolved along with/just after brackets, before ÷ and ×.

question: 83 + 46 ÷ 2 − (12 of 3) + 21 − 18 + 32 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 105.

GIVEN

• 83 + 46 ÷ 2 − (12 of 3) + 21 − 18 + 32

SOLUTION

• 'of' and division first: 12 of 3 = 36; 46 ÷ 2 = 23

• 83 + 23 − 36 + 21 − 18 + 32 = 83 + 23 = 106; 106 − 36 = 70; 70 + 21 = 91; 91 − 18 = 73; 73 + 32 = 105.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 83 + 23 + 21 + 32 = 159; negatives: 36 + 18 = 54; 159 − 54 = 105.

NOTE

• Resolve division/'of' before addition and subtraction; equal-priority + and − are evaluated left to right.

question: P and Q started a business by investing a total of Rs. 9,600. If P invested for m months less than Q, then find the value of m given that P's profit share is Rs. 2,400. Also, P invested Rs. 1,600 less than Q, and the total profit earned at the end of the year is Rs. 9,600.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 6.4 months.

GIVEN

• P + Q = Rs. 9,600; P = Q − 1,600; P's profit = Rs. 2,400 of total Rs. 9,600; Q invested for 12 months, P for (12 − m) months.

SOLUTION

• Capitals: Q − 1,600 + Q = 9,600 → 2Q = 11,200 → Q = 5,600, P = 4,000.

• Profit ratio P : Q = 2,400 : 7,200 = 1 : 3.

• Capital × time: [4,000 × (12 − m)] : [5,600 × 12] = 1 : 3

• 3 × 4,000 × (12 − m) = 5,600 × 12 → 12,000(12 − m) = 67,200 → 12 − m = 5.6 → m = 6.4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• P's time = (Q's capital × ratio-factor): since P:Q profit is 1:3 with capitals 4000:5600, P-time/Q-time = (1/3)×(5600/4000) = 7/15; P-time = 12 × 7/15 = 5.6 → m = 12 − 5.6 = 6.4.

NOTE

• In partnership, Profit ∝ Capital × Time. Fix the unstated period as 12 months (a full year) when 'end of the year' is mentioned.

question: A solution of milk and water contains 60% milk. How many litres of pure milk must be added to 40 litres of this solution to make the milk content 75%?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 24 L.

GIVEN

• 40 L solution with 60% milk; add x L pure milk to make milk 75%.

SOLUTION

• Milk = 60% of 40 = 24 L; Water = 16 L (water stays constant).

• New milk = 24 + x, new total = 40 + x. Require (24 + x)/(40 + x) = 0.75

• 24 + x = 30 + 0.75x → 0.25x = 6 → x = 24 L.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Water is fixed at 16 L and must become the 25% part: total = 16 ÷ 0.25 = 64 L; added milk = 64 − 40 = 24 L.

NOTE

• When one component is unchanged, keep it constant and use it as the anchor: new total = unchanged quantity ÷ its new fraction.

question: A solid metallic hemisphere of radius 7 cm is melted and recast into a cone of base radius 7 cm. Find the height of the cone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 14 cm.

GIVEN

• Hemisphere radius = 7 cm melted into a cone of base radius = 7 cm.

SOLUTION

• Volume conserved: (2/3)πr³ = (1/3)πR²h, with r = R = 7.

• (2/3)π(7)³ = (1/3)π(7)²h → 2 × 7 = h → h = 14 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• When base radius of cone = hemisphere radius, height = 2r directly = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

NOTE

• Recasting keeps volume equal. Hemisphere = (2/3)πr³, Cone = (1/3)πR²h; equate to find the unknown.

question: A hollow spherical shell has an external diameter of 36 cm and an internal diameter of 28 cm. It is melted and recast into spherical balls, each of radius 2 cm. Find the total number of balls formed and the total surface area of all the balls formed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 386, 6176π cm².

GIVEN

• Shell: external radius R = 18 cm, internal radius r = 14 cm; small balls radius = 2 cm.

SOLUTION

• Shell volume = (4/3)π(18³ − 14³) = (4/3)π(5832 − 2744) = (4/3)π(3088).

• One ball = (4/3)π(2³) = (4/3)π(8). Number = 3088 ÷ 8 = 386.

• Total surface area = 386 × 4π(2²) = 386 × 16π = 6176π cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Number = (R³ − r³)/(ball radius)³ = (5832 − 2744)/8 = 386; then × 4π(2²) gives area.

NOTE

• Number of small spheres = (volume of solid)/(volume of one sphere); the (4/3)π cancels, leaving a ratio of cubes.

question: A square and a rectangle have equal perimeters. If the rectangle is 54 cm by 20 cm, find the area of the square.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1369 cm².

GIVEN

• Rectangle 54 cm × 20 cm; square perimeter = rectangle perimeter.

SOLUTION

• Rectangle perimeter = 2(54 + 20) = 148 cm.

• Square side = 148 ÷ 4 = 37 cm.

• Area = 37² = 1369 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Square side = (l + b)/2 = (54 + 20)/2 = 37; area = 37² = 1369.

NOTE

• For equal perimeters, square side = half the sum of rectangle's length and breadth.

question: A rectangular sheet measures 40 cm in length and 25 cm in width. A right-angled triangle with base 12 cm and height 8 cm is cut off from one corner of the rectangle. Find the area of the remaining sheet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 952 cm².

GIVEN

• Rectangle 40 cm × 25 cm; right triangle base 12 cm, height 8 cm cut off.

SOLUTION

• Rectangle area = 40 × 25 = 1000 cm².

• Triangle area = (1/2) × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

• Remaining = 1000 − 48 = 952 cm².

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract half the base×height rectangle: 1000 − 48 = 952 directly.

NOTE

• Remaining area = whole area − cut-out area; a right triangle's area = ½ × base × height.

question: A triangle has an area of 240 cm². If the base is increased by 20% and the corresponding height decreased by 10%, find the percentage change in the area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 8%.

GIVEN

• Base +20%, height −10%; original area = 240 cm².

SOLUTION

• Area ∝ base × height. New factor = 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08.

• Change = 1.08 − 1 = 0.08 = +8% (area increases).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Net % = a + b + ab/100 = 20 + (−10) + (20×−10)/100 = 10 − 2 = 8%.

NOTE

• For two successive percentage changes a% and b%: net % = a + b + (ab/100). The base value (240) is not needed.

question: The area of an equilateral triangle is 81√3 cm². Find its side and altitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Side = 18 cm, Altitude = 9√3 cm.

GIVEN

• Equilateral triangle, area = 81√3 cm².

SOLUTION

• Area = (√3/4)a² = 81√3 → a² = 324 → a = 18 cm.

• Altitude = (√3/2)a = (√3/2) × 18 = 9√3 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• From (√3/4)a² = 81√3, cancel √3: a²/4 = 81 → a = 18; altitude is always (√3/2)×side.

NOTE

• Equilateral triangle: Area = (√3/4)·side², Altitude = (√3/2)·side.

question: A 180 m long train crosses a platform in 36 seconds and a signal pole in 12 seconds. Find the length of the platform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 360 m.

GIVEN

• Train length = 180 m; crosses pole in 12 s, platform in 36 s.

SOLUTION

• Speed = 180 ÷ 12 = 15 m/s.

• In 36 s distance = 15 × 36 = 540 m = train + platform.

• Platform = 540 − 180 = 360 m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Platform = speed × (extra time) = 15 × (36 − 12) = 15 × 24 = 360 m.

NOTE

• Crossing a pole covers only the train's length; crossing a platform covers train + platform. Speed from the pole timing applies throughout.

question: A man walks from his home to a park at 4 km/h and returns along the same route at 6 km/h. If the total time taken for the entire trip is 1 hour. Find the distance between his home and the park.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2.4 km.

GIVEN

• Onward speed 4 km/h, return speed 6 km/h; total time = 1 hour; let one-way distance = d.

SOLUTION

• d/4 + d/6 = 1 → (3d + 2d)/12 = 1 → 5d/12 = 1 → d = 2.4 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Average speed = (2×4×6)/(4+6) = 48/10 = 4.8 km/h; total distance = 4.8 × 1 = 4.8 km; one way = 4.8 ÷ 2 = 2.4 km.

NOTE

• For equal distances at two speeds, average speed = 2ab/(a+b) (harmonic mean).

question: Two cyclists start toward each other from towns A and B, which are 150 km apart. Cyclist A leaves A at 6:00 a.m. with a speed of 20 km/h. Cyclist B leaves B at 7:00 a.m. and they meet at 9:00 a.m. Find the speed of cyclist B (in km/h), rounded to two decimals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 45.00 km/h.

GIVEN

• Distance AB = 150 km; A: 20 km/h from 6:00 a.m.; B from 7:00 a.m.; meet at 9:00 a.m.

SOLUTION

• A travels 6:00 to 9:00 = 3 h → 3 × 20 = 60 km.

• Remaining for B = 150 − 60 = 90 km; B travels 7:00 to 9:00 = 2 h.

• Speed of B = 90 ÷ 2 = 45.00 km/h.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• B's distance = total − (A's speed × A's time) = 150 − 60 = 90; ÷ B's 2 h = 45 km/h.

NOTE

• Account for the head-start: A runs 1 hour longer. When they meet, the sum of both distances equals the total separation.

GIVEN

• 10 2/3 + 3 1/6 − 5 5/6 − 2 1/3

SOLUTION

• Convert to sixths: 64/6 + 19/6 − 35/6 − 14/6.

• = (64 + 19 − 35 − 14)/6 = 34/6 = 17/3 = 5 2/3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Separate wholes and fractions: (10 + 3 − 5 − 2) = 6 whole; (2/3 + 1/6 − 5/6 − 1/3) = (4 + 1 − 5 − 2)/6 = −2/6 = −1/3; 6 − 1/3 = 5 2/3.

NOTE

• Take the LCM of denominators (here 6) once; keep signs with each numerator to avoid slips.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2/15.

GIVEN

• 1/15 + 1/35 + 1/63 + ..... + 1/195

SOLUTION

• Factor denominators: 15=3·5, 35=5·7, 63=7·9, 99=9·11, 143=11·13, 195=13·15.

• Each term 1/(n(n+2)) = ½(1/n − 1/(n+2)); the series telescopes.

• Sum = ½(1/3 − 1/15) = ½ × (5 − 1)/15 = ½ × 4/15 = 2/15.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For consecutive odd products, sum = ½(1/first − 1/last-factor) = ½(1/3 − 1/15) = 2/15.

NOTE

• 1/(n(n+2)) = ½[1/n − 1/(n+2)]; middle terms cancel, leaving only the first and last.

question: 4 × 0.5 + 3.5 × 0.2 + 5 × 0.3 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4.2.

GIVEN

• 4 × 0.5 + 3.5 × 0.2 + 5 × 0.3

SOLUTION

• 4 × 0.5 = 2.0; 3.5 × 0.2 = 0.7; 5 × 0.3 = 1.5.

• Sum = 2.0 + 0.7 + 1.5 = 4.2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Do each product mentally (half of 4, one-fifth of 3.5, 1.5) and add: 2 + 0.7 + 1.5 = 4.2.

NOTE

• Multiplication precedes addition (BODMAS). ×0.5 halves a number; ×0.2 is one-fifth; ×0.3 is three-tenths.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 0.09.

GIVEN

• [(0.5)⁴ − (0.4)⁴] ÷ [(0.5)² + (0.4)²]

SOLUTION

• Numerator = (0.5² − 0.4²)(0.5² + 0.4²) using a² − b² = (a−b)(a+b) with a=0.5², b=0.4².

• Cancel (0.5² + 0.4²): expression = 0.5² − 0.4² = 0.25 − 0.16 = 0.09.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Recognise (a²−b²)/(a+b) pattern: answer is just a − b = 0.25 − 0.16 = 0.09; no fourth powers needed.

NOTE

• x⁴ − y⁴ = (x² − y²)(x² + y²); dividing by (x² + y²) leaves (x² − y²).

question: The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 143. Which of the following is the larger of the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• Two consecutive odd numbers with product 143.

SOLUTION

• 143 lies between 11² =121 and 13² =169, so factors are 11 and 13.

• 11 × 13 = 143 → larger number = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• √143 ≈ 11.96, so the pair straddling it is 11 and 13; larger is 13.

NOTE

• For a product of two close numbers, the value is near its square root; pick the consecutive odd pair around √(product).

question: The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 255. Which of the following is the larger of the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 17.

GIVEN

• Two consecutive odd numbers with product 255.

SOLUTION

• 255 lies between 15² =225 and 17² =289, so factors are 15 and 17.

• 15 × 17 = 255 → larger number = 17.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• √255 ≈ 15.97, so the pair around it is 15 and 17; larger is 17.

NOTE

• The two factors of a near-square product sit just below and above its square root; here √255 ≈ 16.
